free_tier.stated: Empanelled AI cloud services at a subsidy of 'maximum up to 40%', borne by the IndiaAI mission, on a published average of 'approximately Rs 65 per GPU per hour' across 38,231 onboarded GPUs from 14 service providers. Requests of 5,000 GPU hours or fewer, with 50 GPUs or fewer, and with no subsidy sought, skip the PMEC committee and are approved by an institutional verifier or a MeitY Startup Hub CoE.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The 40% is a discount on an empanelled provider's list price, so it composes with the provider's own trial rather than replacing it: the same GPU appears at E2E Networks, NxtGen and Yotta, and a user can price the undiscounted lane directly with those vendors while the subsidy is unavailable.

notes: Three candidate readings of the gate were tested. (a) Indian nationality is required: the policy never states a nationality test, so refuted. (b) A company is required: refuted for the 3.6 early-stage-startup path, which names only four years of founder experience and an endorsement, no incorporation document. (c) An Indian institutional email is required: confirmed at 4.1, and it is what actually stops a user, because APAAR IDs are issued by Indian institutions and the CoE endorsement chain runs through MeitY. Section 3.6 is therefore the only lane that a foreign individual might argue into, and it is decided by a discretionary endorsement rather than a document, so the verdict stays fails-identity and the open question is whether IndiaAI accepts a non-Indian organisation email at registration.
